reason: E1 shows ML potentials can achieve near-DFT accuracy for a refractory high-entropy alloy, supporting the first premise. E2 demonstrates that vibrational entropy (including anharmonicity) is well captured from displacement covariances in AIMD for Al and Na, supporting the second premise. However, no cited evidence addresses active learning for anharmonic regions, enhanced sampling with ML potentials, or the claimed speedup, leaving three key premises unsupported.
premises: ML potentials trained on a subset of configurations can reproduce DFT-level forces and energies for multicomponent systems
Vibrational entropy can be accurately captured from atomic displacement covariances in AIMD
Active learning can refine the training set to cover anharmonic regions
Enhanced sampling (umbrella integration) can reconstruct free-energy landscapes from ML potentials
The combined approach yields an order-of-magnitude speedup over full AIMD or TOR-TILD
